cases.name: failed shared write preserves prior value

contract: After successful in-process key replacement/removal, older shared/file reads cannot return or cache the superseded key. Reads finishing before commit retain existing overlap semantics.

implementation.revision: per-provider counter captured before async reads and advanced with committed cache/sessionOnly state before final writer status lookup
implementation.guards: after shared-key await and after encrypted-file/decrypt attempt, including its caught errors
implementation.mismatch: return latest successfully published cache value, including explicit null; do not reread or wait for the write queue
implementation.failure: existing failed persistence/cache semantics retained; no transactional rollback claim

decision.independentProposals: Boris and Nadia independently proposed per-provider revisions and avoiding read queue reentrancy
decision.challenge: Direct committed-cache return vs another async read; final status await boundary; delayed file rejection; partial persistence
decision.support: Both support bounded current-cache return after successful commit. Locking reads behind keyWrites would deadlock the guarded setup-save callback.
decision.review: Boris inspected actual final diff and found no blocker. Shared adapter catches errors to null, while file/decrypt caught failures also pass revision guard.
decision.ownership: Morgan implemented; reviewers made no edits

checks.privateFiles: replacement files mode0600 in all six cold-file/rejection cases
checks.unitTests: not run; no unit framework or persistent test harness added

limitations: Actual shared-Keychain adapter and personal entries are not accessed; shared values are isolated in memory. Earlier dated OS-adapter evidence is unchanged.
The basic before/after programs use separate native processes. The additional matrix uses fresh storage-module instances and disposable directories in one native process, not a restart per case.
SafeStorage encryption/decryption and private files are actual. Encryption-unavailable state and delayed file rejection are injected only in the temporary fixture.

Failure preservation case rejects the shared write before changing it. Shared success followed by local persistence failure retains existing non-transactional semantics; no rollback or exhaustive partial-failure pass is claimed.

The first direct ESM fixture did not reach readiness. Its exact owned process was terminated; the successful bootstrap imports after app readiness. No result is taken from that terminal startup attempt.
Final fixture hashes include later hold/failure/availability branches used by the matrix; they do not retroactively hash the initial fixture revision.
No new UI, full OS-adapter, VoiceOver, audible-quality, listener or live-provider validation.
